_doc: Argentina, written by hand for the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-12). Buenos Aires and Patagonia are in todo.json.

areas.season: Subtropical: hot and humid, 30–35 °C from December to February with storms; mild from April to October. The falls are fullest after rain.
areas.sleep: Puerto Iguazú town, 20 minutes from the park by bus or taxi; a hotel inside the park lets you see the falls before the gates open.

items.name: Three Borders landmark at sunset
items.why: Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay meet where the Iguazú joins the Paraná.

items.name: The Argentine side: Devil's Throat, Upper and Lower circuits
items.best: Be at the gate when it opens at 08:00
items.book: Park ticket online; the boat under the falls (Gran Aventura) a day ahead
items.why: Walkways right over and under 275 falls; at the Devil's Throat half the river drops into the mist at your feet.

steps.note: first trains go before the groups
2 h, falls from below, rainbows in the spray

extras: Validate your ticket at the exit for half price on a second day in a row.
A dry bag for the phone; quick-dry clothes and sandals with straps.
Coatis snatch food out of hands and bags: eat inside the fenced areas.

items.name: The Brazilian side, the panorama
items.why: The whole width of the falls in one view, the Argentine side opposite. Passport for the border.

steps.what: Cross the border with your passport
The 1.2 km trail along the canyon
Platform into the Devil's Throat spray

extras: Parque das Aves, a bird park by the Brazilian gate, is an easy extra hour.

items.name: Full moon walk to the Devil's Throat
items.why: A few nights a month, around full moon, a guided night walk to the falls in moonlight.

extras: Pesos in cash help in town; the park takes cards.
The falls are the same price both sides, but different money: Argentine pesos one side, Brazilian reais the other.

areas.season: Dry and sunny from April to November; rain and storms from December to March. The city is at 1,150 m.
areas.sleep: In the centre, near Plaza 9 de Julio, or a farmhouse on the edge of town.

items.name: A peña: folk music over dinner
items.why: Guitars, bombos and zambas at the tables, empanadas and local wine. Salta's best night out.

items.name: Salta's centre, the MAAM, and San Bernardo hill by cable car
items.best: Tuesday to Sunday: the MAAM closes on Mondays
items.why: Colonial churches, the museum of the Inca children found on Llullaillaco, and the city from its hill, then a peña.

steps.what: Plaza 9 de Julio and the Cathedral
MAAM, the high mountain archaeology museum
Cable car up Cerro San Bernardo
steps.note: walk down the 1,070 steps if your knees agree

items.name: Cafayate through the Quebrada de las Conchas
items.why: Red rock canyons, the Garganta del Diablo and the Anfiteatro, then high-altitude wine (torrontés) in Cafayate.

steps.what: Quebrada de las Conchas: the Garganta del Diablo and the Anfiteatro

extras: The Anfiteatro has great acoustics: musicians often play there.
Better still: sleep in Cafayate and return through Cachi on the Ruta 40.

items.name: Cachi by the Cuesta del Obispo and the cactus park
items.why: A road of hairpins into the clouds, forests of giant cardón cactus, and a white village at 2,280 m.

items.name: Salinas Grandes and Purmamarca
items.why: A white salt flat at 3,450 m and the Hill of Seven Colours. Better from a night in the Quebrada.

extras: Siesta: many shops close from about 13:00 to 17:00. Dinner starts after 21:00.
The Tren a las Nubes now runs only a short section from San Antonio de los Cobres; check the days.

areas.season: Dry and sunny from April to November; summer rain from December to March. Tilcara is at 2,460 m, Humahuaca at 2,940 m.
areas.sleep: Tilcara has the most life; Purmamarca is tiny and lovely under its hill.

items.name: Pucará de Tilcara and the Garganta del Diablo walk
items.why: A rebuilt pre-Inca hill fort with cactus, then a walk up a red gorge to a waterfall.

items.name: Purmamarca's Hill of Seven Colours and the Salinas Grandes
items.best: Be in Purmamarca early: the hill gets the morning sun
items.why: The striped hill in the morning light, then up the Cuesta de Lipán to a white salt flat at 3,450 m.

steps.note: 3 km loop around the coloured hills

steps.what: Up the Cuesta de Lipán, 4,170 m
Lunch back in Purmamarca: llama, quinoa

items.name: Hornocal, the Fourteen Colours, from Humahuaca
items.best: Afternoon, when the sun lights the face
items.why: A ridge of zigzag pink, green and ochre stripes at 4,350 m, above Humahuaca.

steps.what: Humahuaca: the stairs to the Independence monument
Up the gravel road to Hornocal
The viewpoint; walk down a little for the close view

items.name: Maimará's Painter's Palette
items.why: Painted hills over a hillside cemetery, from the main road.

extras: Carnival in the Quebrada (February or March) is wild and joyful: book rooms early.
The altitude climbs fast: Tilcara 2,460 m, the salt flats 3,450 m, Hornocal 4,350 m.

areas.season: Sunny almost every day; hot summers, cold dry winters. The harvest festival (Vendimia) is in early March.
areas.sleep: Mendoza city for restaurants, or a winery lodge in Luján de Cuyo or the Uco valley.

items.name: Parque San Martín and Cerro de la Gloria
items.why: A huge park of plane trees and canals, and the hill with the monument to the Andes army.

items.name: Wine by bike in Maipú
items.why: Flat roads between wineries and olive oil makers, on a rented bike.

items.name: Uco Valley wineries under the Andes
items.why: Modern wineries at 1,000–1,500 m with the snowy Andes behind the vines. Long lunches.

items.name: The high Andes road to Aconcagua
items.best: A clear day; the pass closes with snow in winter
items.why: Up the old road to Chile: Potrerillos lake, Uspallata, the Puente del Inca and the highest peak outside Asia.

steps.what: Aconcagua park, Laguna de Horcones walk

extras: Siesta: shops close from about 13:00 to 17:00; dinner after 21:00.
Most wineries need a booking, even for a tasting.
